elements.element: Customer has no obligation to disclose more favourable third-party commercial offers to Vendor before engaging another provider.
elements.evidence: The operative clause states that Customer “need not disclose and match” such offers, so it no longer imposes a disclosure duty.

elements.element: Customer has no obligation to match or extend more favourable third-party commercial offers to Vendor before engaging another provider.
elements.evidence: The operative clause states that Customer “need not disclose and match” such offers, removing the original matching obligation.

elements.element: Any MFN or right-to-match obligation burdening Customer is confined to a specifically defined product.
elements.evidence: No Customer-burdening MFN or right-to-match obligation remains, so the condition requiring a product limitation is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any MFN or right-to-match obligation burdening Customer lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: No Customer-burdening MFN or right-to-match obligation remains, so there is no duration exceeding the fallback limit.

elements.element: Any MFN or right-to-match obligation burdening Customer applies only to reasonably comparable offers and excludes materially non-comparable offers.
elements.evidence: No Customer-burdening MFN or right-to-match obligation remains, so the comparison condition is demonstrably absent.

result.reason: The operative redline eliminates the original Customer-burdening disclosure and matching obligation and therefore reaches the preferred position. The fallback limitations are also satisfied because no MFN obligation remains to which product, duration, or comparability limits would need to apply. The change is narrowly targeted and adds no unrelated term. Drafting quality is weak, however: “need not disclose and match” is less precise than deleting the clause or stating that Customer has no obligation to “disclose or match,” because negating a conjunction can create avoidable ambiguity.
